question.leadin: Name these people who all formulated their own law codes.
question.text: This Athenian created Athens' first constitution, whose harshness gave rise to a word meaning "marked by extreme severity or cruelty."
question.clue: This man was given jurisdiction after Cylon tried to seize power, and the orator Demades joked that this man wrote in blood rather than in ink.

swap.text: Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.
swap.clue: This site of the Propylaea also featured six women taking the place of columns on its Caryatid Porch.

question.leadin: Give the following about famously terse replies in history.
question.text: After subduing Theban and Athenian forces, this Macedonian king and father of Alexander the Great sent an envoy to Sparta, saying "Surrender now, because if we invade, we will kill you and tear down your city." Sparta's one-word reply, "If.", convinced this man to leave Sparta alone.
question.answerHtml: Philip II of Macedon (prompt on partial answer)
question.clue: This leader was killed by a man that Cleitarchus claims had been sexually abused by Attalus.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about historians of the ancient world.
swap.text: Despite telling tales of giant ants and massive armies, this Greek is known as the "Father of Histories" for his work the Histories, which details the Persian Wars in addition to providing interesting if not accurate ethnographies of various classical peoples.
swap.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

question.leadin: Pericles gave the Funeral Oration during this war.
question.text: Name this war which Athens and the Delian League fought against the rest of much of the namesake peninsula in Greece.
question.clue: One side in this war laid siege to Melos, where a dialogue apocryphally occurred containing the aphorism "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must."

swap.leadin: This civilization's pottery included Vasiliki ware and Kamares ware.
swap.text: Name this civilization, which Sir Arthur Evans distinguished from the later Mycenaean Civilization. Its primary script is the undeciphered Linear A.
swap.clue: One of this civilization's palaces is where the mysterious Phaistos disc was found.

question.leadin: The losers of this battle were betrayed by Ephialtes.
question.text: Name this battle in which a group of Spartan warriors led by Leonidas defended a narrow pass against the Persian forces of Xerxes I.
question.clue: During this battle, a force including Demophilus' Thespians was attacked from behind after Ephialtes ("eh-fi-AL-tees") revealed a Phocian-guarded path to Xerxes.

swap.text: This Greek city on an isthmus had an ancient greased track called the diolkos replaced with a canal in the 19th century.
swap.clue: According to Herodotus, this city provided 40 ships at the Battle of Salamis, the second most after Athens.

question.leadin: A failed rebellion on this island in 1770 was led by a shipbuilder named Daskalogiannis.
question.text: Identify this island where the Venetians surrendered at Candia after a lengthy siege in 1669. The Phaistos Disc was found on this island, which in ancient times was home to a bull-jumping cult.
question.clue: Modern archaeologists no longer agree that a civilization on this island collapsed after an eruption of Thera.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about mercenaries in the ancient world.
swap.text: This large island provided slingers to Mediterranean armies for a fee. After a failed Antigonid siege of this island, its citizens built a namesake colossus depicting Helios.
swap.clue: After being expelled from Jerusalem in the 14th century, the Knights of St. John made this their base, although were forced to find a new home after it was sacked in 1522 by Suleiman the Magnificent.

question.leadin: A gold funerary mask found at this site was dubbed the "Mask of Agamemnon" by Heinrich Schliemann.
question.text: Name this archeological site. It names a phase of the Greek bronze age which followed the Minoan civilization and was likely destroyed by the Dorian invasion.
question.clue: Along with the nearby Tiryns, this city is the most famous example of limestone Cyclopean walls, which the Lion Gate permits entry through.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the early Dark Ages.
swap.text: Historians look at the "migration" of people known by this term, which included the Huns and Ostrogoths. The Romans used this term to refer to the "uncivilized" tribes of people living outside their borders.
swap.clue: A word that is probably derived from the Greek word rha plus the Greek root of this word is traditionally used by stage actors to imitate the sound of indistinct conversation.

question.leadin: This tribe's dialect of Greek related to Attic was spoken on the Cyclades, Euboea, and by Greeks around the Hellespont.
question.text: Name this Greek tribe, who settled the region around Ephesus. Two tyrants from Miletus led people of this tribe in a revolt in 499 BCE after Aristogaras failed to take Naxos.

swap.text: In the 220s BCE-era Cleomenean War, the Achaean League fought Sparta and this allied polis that expanded into perioikic Margana and Amphidolis. Circa 400 BCE, Sparta fought this polis for banning it from a temple of Zeus.
swap.answerHtml: Elis [or Ilia or Eleia or Elida; prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, Olympiá by asking “what polis was that sanctuary controlled by?”]
swap.clue: This city constructed its Prytaneion near the Pelopion in one sanctuary during the sixth century BC in order to emphasise this polis' control over it.

question.text: The siege of Syracuse began after a power struggle resulting from the death of this ninety-year old tyrant, who had managed to keep Syracuse out of the First Punic War by signing a 263 BC treaty with Rome.
question.clue: This tyrant ruled Syracuse until his death in 216 BC, when he was succeeded by his grandson Hieronymus.

swap.leadin: Note to moderator: Please do not reveal the alternative answers to the first bonus part unless they are the given responses, as they give away the second bonus part. Thanks. Despite not strictly fitting the definition of this group's name, Pyrrhus of Epirus is counted among them.
swap.text: Name these generals who divided up the Hellenistic Empire at the Partition of Babylon. Many of its members would unite to defeat another member, Antigonus the One-eyed, at the Battle of Ipsus.
swap.answerHtml: Diadochi [or descriptive answers such as successors to Alexander the Great; accept alternatives to Alex the Great such as Alexander III of Macedon, Alexander Magnus, etc.; prompt on successors and on incomplete versions of Alexander’s name such as Alexander or Alexander of Macedon if a descriptive answer is given]
swap.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

question.text: A feature of the Magonid army was the existence of a small group of elite fighters with this name; this name also belonged to an elite Theban unit.
question.clue: This group was unusually put on the left side of an army during a battle in which Cleombrotus's army was destroyed by Epaminondas.

swap.text: Polybius singled out this alliance of ancient Greece for practicing piracy. This alliance defeated the Boeotian League at Chaeronea in 245 BCE and it controlled Delphi for much of the 3rd century BCE.
swap.clue: The losers at Paxos also included this Greek confederacy that, like their Illyrian frenemies, had a reputation for piracy. This alliance based at Thermos consistently backed Rome against Macedon, including at Cynoscephalae.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about wars from Archaic Greek history that we don't really know anything about, FTPE.
question.text: A series of wars in the eighth and seventh centuries led to Sparta's conquest of this region of the Peloponnese, whose inhabitants were the original Helots.
question.clue: This Peloponnesian region that fought three wars, including two in the Archaic Period, with a neighboring polis. Demand for this region's fertile land, or kleroi, likely helped cause the first of those conflicts.

swap.text: Twenty-eight elders and two hereditary kings made up this Spartan senate, which Lycurgus instituted in his Great Rhetra. In the convoluted scheme of Spartan government, this body consulted with the ephors and prepared motions for the Apella to vote on and could also veto motions passed by the Apella.
swap.clue: Lycurgus created this Spartan council of elders, which was made up of people over sixty. Members were elected and served for life.
